arguments.root_cause_statement: The Service search in namespace search selects pods with the label app=search-api, but the only pods that serve the search backend are produced by Deployment search, whose pod template labels them app=search. No pod in the namespace carries app=search-api, so the endpoint controller populates no addresses for the Service and its Endpoints object has no subsets. The Deployment is healthy — both replicas are Running and Ready and the container logs "search: serving on :8080" — which is why the deployment reports 2/2 while every gateway call to the search ClusterIP has nowhere to go, producing the storewide search timeouts the page describes.
arguments.mechanism: The Service search in namespace search has .spec.selector set to {"app": "search-api"} while the pods that back it are labelled app=search, so the selector matches zero pods; the endpoint controller therefore writes an Endpoints object search with no subsets, and connections to the Service's ClusterIP 10.96.24.225:8080 have no backend to be routed to.

evidence.claim: The paged Service has no endpoint addresses while both search pods are Running and Ready.
The Service selector asks for label app=search-api.
The Deployment that runs the search backend labels its pods app=search, not app=search-api.
The Endpoints object for the Service contains no subsets, i.e. no addresses.
The web gateway's calls to the search Service never complete.
evidence.quote: gateway: search fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)

evidence.claim: The search backend process is itself healthy and listening on the Service's target port 8080.

ruled_out.alternative: The search backend pods are crashed or not serving, so the Service has no ready endpoints.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both replicas are Running with ready=True and zero restarts, and the container logs show it listening on port 8080.

ruled_out.alternative: The web-gateway workload is misconfigured (bad image, bad script mount) and is the thing that must change.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The gateway pod is Running and Ready with its scripts ConfigMap mounted and it is successfully attempting calls; its failures are connection-level against the search Service.

ruled_out.alternative: The Service targets the wrong port, so traffic reaches pods but nothing listens.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service targetPort 8080 matches the container port 8080 the backend listens on; the failure is that no address exists at all.

verification.command: kubectl -n search get service search -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'
kubectl -n search get endpoints search -o yaml
